context: In France a cell phone is 'un portable' or 'un smartphone'.
Also spelled 'les clefs'. 'J'ai perdu mes clés' = I lost my keys.
Literally 'carry-leaf'. 'Le porte-monnaie' = coin purse.
'Un sac à main' = handbag; 'un sac à dos' = backpack.
'Un cahier' is the school exercise book.
'Un crayon' is a pencil, not a crayon (which is 'un crayon de couleur').
'Un ordinateur portable' = a laptop.
'Montrer' = to show; 'la montre' = the thing that shows the time.
Always plural, like 'les lunettes'.
'Para' (against) + 'pluie' (rain).
Both feminine. 'À table !' = Dinner's ready!
'Ouvrir la fenêtre' = to open the window.
Informally: 'la bagnole'. In Québec: 'le char'.
Short for 'vélocipède'. Many French cities have bike-sharing systems.

front: la bouteille / le verre / la tasse
context: 'Une tasse de thé' = a cup of tea; 'une tasse à thé' = a teacup.
Casual. More standard: 'Qu'est-ce que c'est ?'
The standard question to ask what something is. Answer: 'C'est un…' / 'C'est une…'
'C'est un/une' introduces a thing; 'ce sont des' for plurals.
'Être à quelqu'un' = to belong to someone. Answer: 'C'est à moi' = it's mine.
Also: c'est à toi (yours), à lui (his), à elle (hers), à nous (ours).

front: C'est mon livre, pas le tien.
context: 'Le tien / la tienne' = yours (informal). 'Le vôtre / la vôtre' = yours (formal or plural).
'Mes' (my) is plural: mon (m), ma (f), mes (pl). Before a vowel: mon amie.

front: Mes clés sont sur la table.
back: My keys are on the table.
context: 'Sur' = on; 'sous' = under; 'dans' = in.

front: Le chargeur est dans mon sac.
back: The charger is in my bag.
context: 'Dans' = inside something.

front: Le chat dort sous le lit.
back: The cat is sleeping under the bed.
context: Don't confuse 'sous' [soo] (under) with 'sur' [sür] (on).
'Avoir besoin de' = to need. Very useful at A1.

front: Tu peux me prêter ton parapluie ?
back: Can you lend me your umbrella?
context: 'Prêter' = to lend; 'emprunter' = to borrow.

front: Il y a des livres partout !
context: 'Partout' = everywhere; 'nulle part' = nowhere.
'Neuf/neuve' = brand new; 'nouveau/nouvelle' = new (to me, different).

front: Je cherche mon portable, tu l'as vu ?
pronunciation: [zhuh shersh mohn por-TAH-bluh, tü lah VÜ]
back: I'm looking for my phone, have you seen it?
context: 'Chercher' = to look for (no 'pour' needed).
